subject: Post-call recap: residency constraints and deployment fit for Atlas Health
messages:
From: KarThik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Sana Rao <sana@atlashealth.com>, Tom Evans <tevans@atlashealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Jan 2027 15:02:00 -0500
Subject: Post-call recap: residency constraints and deployment fit for Atlas Health

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can scope next steps:

Key constraints we heard
- EU: patient PHI for EU residents must remain in EU-hosted infrastructure (data-at-rest + processing).
- APAC: a subset of your enterprise contracts (AU) require data to remain in-country or in an approved APAC region.
- Cross-region access: Atlas has internal reporting that may need cross-border reads for aggregated metrics, but you can accept replicated non-PHI aggregates in US/EU.

How this maps to deployment modes (initial thoughts)
- Hosted API (Redwood-hosted in EU region): good fit for EU-only traffic where Atlas can accept Redwood-managed keys and region tenancy. Lower operational overhead.
- Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs in EU): strong fit if you want isolation and a contract-backed SLA plus the ability to control autoscaling patterns; easier to meet stricter contractual SLAs.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): likely required for Australian contracts that mandate local hosting + key control. Also the path for full network isolation and your own KMS/HSM.

Open questions for us to validate (please reply inline):
1) Approx % of traffic (by monthly tokens) that is EU PHI vs APAC-bound PHI vs non-PII global traffic?
2) For APAC contracts that require in-country hosting, which countries are strict (Australia only?) and timelines for those contracts?
3) Are you able to accept Redwood-managed KMS for EU, or do you require customer-managed keys across all regions?
4) Any procurement or security questionnaires we should start pulling SOC2/KMS evidence for now?

Attachments: I attached a short residency-eval-matrix.xlsx that maps deployment modes to compliance and ops tradeoffs.

Proposed next steps
- If you confirm the points above, we’ll schedule a 30-min technical deep-dive (Marissa + Ben on our side) to walk the residency matrix and draft a recommended pilot architecture (Hosted EU + Private APAC pilot).
- We’ll prepare SOC2 excerpts, KMS integration notes, and a sample SLA for Dedicated if you want pricing/commitment estimates.

Thanks — want to keep this tight so we can move to procurement if it checks out.

-Karthik

Subject: Re: Post-call recap: residency constraints and deployment fit for Atlas Health

Thanks Karthik — helpful summary. A few clarifications inline: 

> EU: patient PHI for EU residents must remain in EU-hosted infrastructure (data-at-rest + processing).
Yes, mandatory for our EU patient data; our DPA requires EU residency and we would need contract language that specifies region.

> APAC: a subset of your enterprise contracts (AU) require data to remain in-country or in an approved APAC region.
This is accurate — Australia is the only APAC market with hard in-country hosting for now. Singapore is preferred for non-AU APAC traffic but not mandated.

Questions from our side:
- KMS: we prefer customer-managed keys for APAC/AU contracts. For EU PHI we can consider Redwood-managed keys if the key lifecycles meet our policy, but we will need details.
- Procurement timeline: we’re aiming to have a pilot in Q2; procurement typically needs a security package and a statement on where keys live.

Tom and I are happy to do the technical deep dive next week — Tue/Thu mornings AEST work best for us.

Sana Rao
Head of Cloud Integrations | Atlas Health
sana@atlashealth.com | +61 2 9000 1234

Hi Sana / Tom — looping in a couple of technical pointers based on Karthik’s notes and your clarifications.

Short answer recommendation (from an SRE/SE perspective)
- EU PHI: Dedicated capacity in the EU (customer-dedicated GPU pool) gives the best combination of contractual isolation, predictable latency, and easier SOC2/KMS evidence. We can scope an EU-only Dedicated pilot for PHI traffic.
- Australia (AU): Private VPC or on-prem bundle is the most straightforward path for contracts that mandate in-country hosting and customer-managed keys. We support HSM/KMS integrations and can provide deployment automation for an AU VPC.
- Cross-region reporting: For non-PHI aggregates, we recommend asynchronous replication to a global analytics workspace (redacted of PHI) hosted in a US/EU analytics tenant. Live cross-region reads for PHI should be blocked by default.

Notes on KMS and technical support
- EU: Redwood-managed KMS is supported; we provide key usage logs and rotation policies. If you prefer customer-managed keys, we can integrate with your KMS via standard KMIP or cloud-KMS endpoints for Dedicated or Private.
- AU: for in-country legal requirements we recommend customer-managed keys + HSM for auditability.

Attachments I’m sharing: deployment-option-brief.pdf (short architecture sketches) and kms-integration-notes.txt (integration checklist).

If you’re open to the hybrid pilot (EU Dedicated + APAC Private VPC), we can draft a runbook and a constrained-cost estimate for the pilot. Recommend 4-week pilot to validate latency and compliance gates.

Action items (Marissa/Ben/Karthik -> Atlas):
- Atlas to confirm % traffic split by region and specific APAC country list.
- Atlas to confirm whether Redwood-managed KMS is acceptable for EU PHI pilot.
- Redwood to prepare SOC2 excerpts and KMS integration checklist and cost estimate for pilot.

Happy to jump on a call to walk through the attachments.

—
